stories.primary_headline: Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede

primary_source.headline: Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede
primary_source.content: The stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata claimed the lives of 19 people, while 25 others were injured. A senior police officer told PTI that lack of crowd management and misleading announcements following sudden heavy rainfall during Saptami celebrations could have led to the tragic incident. Police also found that the number of police personnel and private security guards deployed at the venue was inadequate, worsening the situation."We have gathered sufficient evidence pointing to gross mismanagement by the puja organisers. There was no clear plan to manage the large number of visitors, and everything was handled verbally. We have collected CCTV camera footage, recorded accounts from locals and eyewitnesses, and corroborated our findings. Security personnel were inadequate," the police officer told PTI.At least 19 dead, 25 others injured in stampede-like situation at Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata"Due to the mismanagement, people tried to escape through the entrance gate during the stampede. Both the gates and the approach road were narrow, which contributed to the accident," he said, adding that announcements regarding entry, exit and crowd movement were misleading, leaving visitors confused during the rush."We have video footage of an announcement asking people to leave the pandal on the grounds that the structure was about to collapse. We are trying to identify who made the announcement and what prompted it," the officer said.Moreover, the locals also claimed that police deployment was inadequate, alleging that personnel were mainly stationed near the VIP entrance.A team of forensic experts visited the pandal on Saturday night and collected evidence from the site, he said."Another team of forensic experts will visit the pandal today to collect further evidence. Officers from our Detective Department will also visit the venue as part of the investigation," he said.The Kolkata Police could question survivors as part of the probe, the IPS officer said."We need first-hand accounts to cross-check the findings based on statements from locals and other eyewitnesses. This will help our investigation," he added.Meanwhile, prohibitory orders under Section 163 have been imposed on roads adjoining the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Sunday morning.The order prohibits gatherings on roads surrounding the venue, which falls under the jurisdiction of Bowbazar Police Station. The restrictions will remain in force until October 20.Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the state government would provide Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job to the family of each deceased victim.He also ordered the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court, to investigate the incident.

brief_bullets: A significant Ukrainian drone swarm targeted critical infrastructure within St. Petersburg and the surrounding Leningrad region, resulting in at least one fatality and fifteen injuries. This coordinated aerial assault marks a notable escalation in the conflict, as Ukrainian forces increasingly project their reach deep into Russian territory to disrupt logistics and domestic stability. Local authorities and emergency services were mobilized to address the widespread impact of the strikes, which have caused substantial alarm among regional officials and the civilian population. By successfully penetrating deep-range air defenses to strike such a high-profile metropolitan area, Ukraine is signaling a shift in its tactical approach, moving beyond frontline engagements to challenge the perceived security of Russia's interior. The incident underscores the growing vulnerability of Russian urban centers to asymmetric warfare and highlights the intensifying nature of the ongoing cross-border hostilities. This attack demonstrates Ukraine's expanding capability to strike deep within Russian territory, forcing Moscow to divert critical air defense assets away from the front lines to protect its major cities. Such operations serve to erode the domestic narrative of Russian security and increase the political cost of the war for the Kremlin.

sources.headline: CJP alleges delay in release of leaders, 4 sureties rejected
sources.content: New Delhi: The bail hearing of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka was "delayed" on Sunday as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) did not arrive at the scheduled time, activist Ratna Singh said and alleged that four sureties had been rejected on "vague" grounds.Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after they entered Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, by scaling its locked gates. The CJP leaders maintained that they had unfurled the national flag and raised slogans.In a post on X, Singh said she had been at the police station since 11 am, while the hearing was scheduled for noon. She said the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP/SEM) had not arrived at the Mandir Marg police station by 4.42 pm.CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde under preventive arrest; likely to be produced before magistrate"This is really concerning. They have rejected 4 sureties till now on vague reasons. They have made people who have FIRs against them for being part of protest as people having criminal antecedents (sic)," Singh alleged.There was no response from police on the allegations.In another post, Singh said, "Unfurling the Indian National Flag is not a crime, and the boys should not remain in custody due to procedural delays."Questioning the functioning of the SEM courts in the national capital, Singh said higher courts had asked authorities to follow the hierarchy and alleged an "absolute misuse of power".On Saturday, the CJP said in a post on X that it had consulted senior advocate Kapil Sibal and warned of legal action if Das and Ranka were not released by Sunday."If Ashu and Saurav are not released by tomorrow, we will pursue legal action against all those who deliberately ensured that they continue to be in illegal custody, especially when they have not committed nor charged with any offence," the outfit had said."The deliberate use of delaying tactics to keep them behind bars cannot go unchallenged. Those responsible will be held accountable," it added.The outfit has been protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the exercise threatens voters' rights.
